accuracyClaim.statement: C5 is a decision-#86 gate_remediation candidate and must never be presented as an accuracy improvement. It captures +1.754% of global relative WAPE against decision #75's 5% floor, which is a fail, and it was adopted only under the remediation class.

currentServedIdentity.note: The C5 method is unchanged; the bundle that serves it is not the one it was first published as. fr_b2ef3d33f398095b was activated by event 7 with a null predecessor and was superseded by event 8 when the decision-#92 field withholding required a replacement bundle. Event 9 activated fr_357575f586905b11 with prior_event_id = 8. Both ids are retained: the historical one is what this candidate record measured, the current one is what serves.

adoption.notUnder: decision #75, whose 5% global floor it does not meet (+1.754%)

structuralChecksEnforcedAtPublication.note: Both were previously asserted in the decision document and never executed. They now run inside publish_forecast_run, so a remediation bundle that fails either cannot be published at all.

adoption.supersedesEarlierRecordOfThisFile: An earlier revision of this file read "Not adopted", which was true of the #75 evaluation and became misleading once #86 was decided. Kept as a corrected record rather than deleted.

decision_75_global_materiality.detail: The 17.053% ceiling was for a perfect cohort fix. C5 captures 1.754% of global relative WAPE, so room existed but C5 does not capture enough of it.

decision_85_per_cohort_coverage.detail: cold-start coverage moved the WRONG WAY: 0.7937 -> 0.7847 global, 0.7785 -> 0.7673 us-new-york. My §4 prediction that a raised centre would lift coverage was wrong. Reason: the comparator is above the champion on only 51.2% of rows but carries more volume (median 8.15 vs 10.09, sum 3,596,857 vs 3,342,805). WAPE is volume-weighted, coverage is row-counted, so blending toward a higher-variance estimator lowers the prediction on the many small rows and lowers P90 with it.

fittedOn: 8 development origins only; final 5 untouched until w frozen

fittedWeights.india-west: 1.0 at h1-h9 falling to 0.25 at h26
fittedWeights.note: w declines monotonically with horizon in both markets. The fit was never told horizons are ordered - it found this per cell independently, which corroborates the long-horizon mechanism rather than assuming it.
fittedWeights.us-new-york: 0.95 at h1 falling to 0.0 at h13-h20, 0.25 at h26

intervalCalibrationVariant.assessment: A band-aid, and decision #84 §5 already forbids adjusting intervals to rescue coverage. A P90 that covers 78% is a miscalibrated quantile model, not a too-narrow one; widening by 2.39x hides that rather than fixing it. Recorded as measured, NOT recommended for adoption.
intervalCalibrationVariant.cost: median width multiplier 2.3927; median cold-start displayed confidence falls 0.6030 -> 0.4065
intervalCalibrationVariant.coverageResult: all six decision-#85 cells PASS: cold-start 0.9156 global, 0.9135 india-west, 0.9174 us-new-york
intervalCalibrationVariant.description: C5 plus a cold-start interval width multiplier fitted per market x horizon on the 8 development origins to reach 0.90 coverage.

See decision #89 for why the input fingerprints moved while the data did not.
verdict: C5 repairs the A1 blocker in every scope and does not satisfy decision #75. It is adopted under decision #86 as a gate-remediation candidate, not as an accuracy improvement, and #86 forbids presenting it as one. The #75 shortfall below is published rather than suppressed.
